name: Ideology of the Chinese Communist Party
summary: The CCP's official ideology is Marxism-Leninism adapted to China, running through Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development and Xi Jinping Thought. Its own documents hold that the Party must lead the state and army, that China is a people's democratic dictatorship at the primary stage of socialism with dominant public ownership alongside a socialist market economy, that class struggle persists but is no longer the main contradiction, and that communism remains the ultimate goal. Foreign policy rests on sovereignty, non-interference and opposition to hegemonism, and the Party treats Taiwan as part of China that it will not promise to leave unreached by force.
scope: The current official line of the Party as set out in its constitution's General Program (2002 text), the 2022 report to the 20th National Congress, the 2021 resolution on the Party's history, and the state constitution as amended in 2018 under which the Party rules. Mao Zedong Thought and Deng Xiaoping Theory count as the Party presents them there. It excludes dissident Marxist, Maoist-revival and liberal reformist currents inside China, and the documents are silent on most social and moral questions, which stay null.
